questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 7]

Consider the function f(x)=−2(x−1)(x+3), for x∈ℝ. The following diagram shows part of the graph of f.

[Diagram: a downward-opening parabola.]

(a) For the graph of f,
(i) find the x-coordinates of the x-intercepts;
(ii) find the coordinates of the vertex. [5]

The function f can be written in the form f(x)=−2(x−h)²+k.

(b) Write down the value of h and the value of k. [2]
questions.solution: (a)(i) The factors give roots x=1 and x=−3. (a)(ii) Their midpoint is x=−1 and f(−1)=8, so the vertex is (−1,8). (b) Thus f=−2(x+1)²+8, so h=−1 and k=8.

questions.accessible_text:
2. [Maximum mark: 4]

Given that dy/dx=cos(x−π/4) and y=2 when x=3π/4, find y in terms of x.

3. [Maximum mark: 5]

The function f is defined by f(x)=(2x+4)/(3−x), where x∈ℝ, x≠3.

(a) Write down the equation of
(i) the vertical asymptote of the graph of f;
(ii) the horizontal asymptote of the graph of f. [2]

(b) Find the coordinates where the graph of f crosses
(i) the x-axis;
(ii) the y-axis. [2]

(c) Sketch the graph of f on the supplied axes. [1]

[Axes: x and y each run approximately from −15 to 15.]
questions.solution: (a)(i) The vertical asymptote is x=3. (a)(ii) The horizontal asymptote is y=−2. (b)(i) The x-intercept is (−2,0). (b)(ii) The y-intercept is (0,4/3). (c) Since f=−2−10/(x−3), the left branch is above y=−2 and tends to +∞ at 3⁻; the right branch is below y=−2 and tends to −∞ at 3⁺.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 5]

Box 1 contains 5 red balls and 2 white balls. Box 2 contains 4 red balls and 3 white balls.

(a) A box is chosen at random and a ball is drawn. Find the probability that the ball is red. [3]

Let A be the event that “box 1 is chosen” and let R be the event that “a red ball is drawn”.

(b) Determine whether events A and R are independent. [2]
questions.solution: (a) P(R)=(1/2)(5/7)+(1/2)(4/7)=9/14. (b) P(A∩R)=5/14 while P(A)P(R)=9/28. These are unequal, so A and R are not independent.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 7]

The function f is defined for all x∈ℝ. The line with equation y=6x−1 is the tangent to the graph of f at x=4.

(a) Write down the value of f′(4). [1]

(b) Find f(4). [1]

The function g is defined for all x∈ℝ, where g(x)=x²−3x and h(x)=f(g(x)).

(c) Find h(4). [2]

(d) Hence find the equation of the tangent to the graph of h at x=4. [3]
questions.summary: Apply chain rule to tangent data.
questions.solution: (a) The tangent gradient gives f′(4)=6. (b) The tangent point gives f(4)=6(4)−1=23. (c) Since g(4)=4, h(4)=f(4)=23. (d) By the chain rule, h′(4)=f′(4)(2·4−3)=30. Thus y−23=30(x−4), or y=30x−97.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 7]

(a) Show that (2x²−5x−3)/(x−1)=2x−3−6/(x−1), x∈ℝ, x≠1. [2]

(b) Hence or otherwise, solve the equation (2sin²(2θ)−5sin(2θ)−3)/(sin(2θ)−1)=0 for 0≤θ≤π, θ≠π/4. [5]
questions.solution: (a) Combining the RHS gives [(2x−3)(x−1)−6]/(x−1)=(2x²−5x−3)/(x−1). (b) Numerator zero: (2sin2θ+1)(sin2θ−3)=0, so sin2θ=−1/2. Hence 2θ=7π/6,11π/6 and θ=7π/12,11π/12.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 16]

A particle P moves along the x-axis. The velocity of P is v m s⁻¹ at time t seconds, where v(t)=4+4t−3t² for 0≤t≤3. When t=0, P is at the origin O.

(a) (i) Find the value of t when P reaches its maximum velocity.
(ii) Show that the distance of P from O at this time is 88/27 metres. [7]

(b) Sketch a graph of v against t, clearly showing any points of intersection with the axes. [4]

(c) Find the total distance travelled by P. [5]
questions.solution: (a)(i) v′=4−6t=0 gives t=2/3. (a)(ii) Displacement is [4t+2t²−t³]₀^(2/3)=88/27 m. (b) The graph is a concave-down parabola starting at (0,4), with vertex (2/3,16/3), crossing at (2,0), and ending at (3,−11). (c) The distances are ∫₀²v dt=8 and |∫₂³v dt|=5, for a total of 13 m.

questions.accessible_text:
8. [Maximum mark: 15]

Consider the function f(x)=aˣ, where x∈ℝ, a∈ℝ⁺ and a>1. The graph of f contains the point (2/3,4).

(a) Show that a=8. [2]

(b) Write down an expression for f⁻¹(x). [1]

(c) Find the value of f⁻¹(32). [3]

(d) Consider the arithmetic sequence log₈27, log₈p, log₈q, log₈125, where p>1 and q>1.
(i) Show that 27, p, q and 125 are four consecutive terms in a geometric sequence.
(ii) Find the value of p and the value of q. [9]
questions.solution: (a) a^(2/3)=4 gives a=8. (b) Thus f⁻¹(x)=log₈x. (c) f⁻¹(32)=log₈32=5/3. (d)(i) Equal logarithmic differences imply equal ratios, so 27,p,q,125 are consecutive terms of a geometric sequence. (d)(ii) Its ratio cubed is 125/27, hence the ratio is 5/3; therefore p=45 and q=75.

questions.accessible_text:
9. [Maximum mark: 14]

Consider a function f with domain a<x<b. The following diagram shows the graph of f′, the derivative of f.

[Graph of f′: x-intercepts at p, 0 and t; local maxima at q and t; a local minimum at r; a<p<q<0<r<t<b. The graph is positive only for p<x<0 and touches, but does not cross, the x-axis at t.]

The graph of f′ has x-intercepts at x=p, x=0 and x=t. There are local maximum points at x=q and x=t and a local minimum point at x=r.

(a) Find all the values of x where the graph of f is increasing. Justify your answer. [2]

(b) Find the value of x where the graph of f has a local maximum. [1]

(c) (i) Find the value of x where the graph of f has a local minimum. Justify your answer.
(ii) Find the values of x where the graph of f has points of inflexion. Justify your answer. [5]

(d) The total area of the region enclosed by the graph of f′ and the x-axis is 20. Given that f(p)+f(t)=4, find the value of f(0). [6]
questions.solution: (a) f increases for p<x<0 because f′>0 there. (b) It has a local maximum at x=0 because f′ changes from positive to negative. (c)(i) It has a local minimum at x=p because f′ changes from negative to positive. (c)(ii) Inflexions occur at the turning points of f′: x=q,r,t, where f″ changes sign. (d) Let A=f(0)−f(p) and B=f(0)−f(t). The total area gives A+B=20, so 2f(0)−[f(p)+f(t)]=20. Hence 2f(0)−4=20 and f(0)=12.
